facts.text: The person making wudhu should face the qiblah and sit on an elevated place so that the water does not splash on him.
When commencing wudhu, Bismillahir Rahmânir Raheem should be recited.
The hands should be washed up to the wrists three times.
The mouth should be rinsed three times and a miswâk should be used.
If there is no miswâk, a thick cloth or the fore-finger could be used so that all the dirt is removed.
If the person is not fasting, he should gargle the mouth thoroughly.
If the person is fasting, he should not gargle thoroughly because water might go down the throat.
The nose should be rinsed three times and cleaned with the left hand.
If the person is fasting, he should not allow the water to go beyond the soft-bone of the nose.
The face should be washed three times from the hair-line till below the chin and from one ear-lobe to the other.
Water must reach below the eye brows so no place remains dry.
The right hand should be washed up to and including the elbows.
The left hand should be washed up to and including the elbows.
Khilâl of the fingers should be made by passing the fingers of one hand through the fingers of the other hand.
If there is a ring or any such jewellery on the fingers, it should be removed so that no part is left dry.
Masah of the head should be made by passing wet hands over the head.
Masah of the ears should be made by inserting the forefingers into the ears and making masah of the back of the ear-lobes with the thumb of each hand.
Masah of the neck should be made with the back of the fingers of both hands.
Masah of the fore-neck/throat should not be made because it is prohibited.
Fresh water need not be used for making masah of the ears.
Whatever water is left over after making masah of the head is sufficient for the ears.
The right foot should be washed up to and including the ankles.
The left foot should be washed up to and including the ankles.
Khilâl of the toes of the feet should be made with the little finger of the left hand.
When making khilâl of the toes, it should commence with the little toe of the right foot and end with the little toe of the left foot.
There are four fardh acts of wudhu.
One fardh act of wudhu is to wash the entire face once.
One fardh act of wudhu is to wash both hands up to and including the elbows once.
One fardh act of wudhu is to make masah of one-quarter of the head once.
One fardh act of wudhu is to wash both feet up to and including the ankles once.
If any fardh act is left out or if a place equal to a hair's breadth is left dry, wudhu will not be complete.
Sunnah acts of wudhu include saying Bismillahir Rahmânir Raheem.
Sunnah acts of wudhu include washing both hands up to the wrists.
Sunnah acts of wudhu include rinsing the mouth.
Sunnah acts of wudhu include washing the nose.
Sunnah acts of wudhu include using miswâk.
Sunnah acts of wudhu include making masah of the entire head.
Sunnah acts of wudhu include washing each part three times.
Sunnah acts of wudhu include making masah of the ears.
Sunnah acts of wudhu include making khilâl of the fingers and toes.
Once the four fardh acts of wudhu are carried out, wudhu will be regarded as complete irrespective of whether one intended to make wudhu.
If at the time of bathing one pours water on the entire body, wudhu will be regarded as complete if the limbs of wudhu get wet.
If someone falls into a well or river or stands in the rain and the limbs of wudhu get wet, wudhu will be regarded as complete.
Wudhu will be complete even if the procedure is altered, such as washing the feet first, then making masah, then washing the hands, and thereafter washing the face.
If the left hand or the left foot is washed first, wudhu will be completed but it will be contrary to being mustahab.
After washing one part, one should not delay washing the next part so long that the first part gets dry.
It is sunnah to pass the hand on the part that is being washed so that no place is left dry.
It is better and mustahab to prepare for wudhu and salât well before the time.
As long as there is no genuine excuse, one should perform wudhu with one's very own hands and should not seek assistance from someone else.
Worldly talk should be avoided while making wudhu.
Bismillah and the kalimah should be read on washing each and every part.
Water should not be wasted even if water is freely available.
Even at the sea-shore, one should not use more than necessary.
One should not use so little water that the parts cannot be washed thoroughly.
The parts should not be washed more than three times.
When washing the face, water should not be splashed with great force.
Water should not be splashed by making hissing sounds.
One should not close one's eyes and mouth very tightly.
If the mouth and eyes are shut so tightly that the lips or eye lashes remain dry, then wudhu will not be regarded as complete.
If rings, bangles, bracelets, etc. are loose enough for water to reach under them, it will still be mustahab to remove them.
If rings, bangles, bracelets, etc. are tight enough that water might not reach under them, it is necessary and wajib to remove them.
For a nose ring, if it is loose it is mustahab to move it.
For a nose ring, if it is tight, it is wajib to move it around while washing the face so water reaches everywhere.
If some dough or similar substance got stuck under the nails and dried so water did not reach there, wudhu will not be complete.
If flour is seen under nails and water did not reach there, water should be poured over it.
If salât was performed prior to pouring water over dried substance under nails, it will be necessary to repeat the salât.
If tinsel or decorative paint is applied on the forehead and not washed thoroughly, but only water is poured over it, wudhu will not be completed.
Decorative paint on the forehead should be removed before washing the face.
After performing wudhu, Surah al-Qadr should be recited.
After performing wudhu, the dua should be recited: "O Allah! Make me of the repentants, and make me of the purified, and include me among Your pious servants."
After performing wudhu, it is preferable to read two rakâts of nafl salât called Tahiyyatul wudhu.
If wudhu was made for a particular salât and the next salât time enters without wudhu breaking, it is permissible to read salât with that same wudhu.
If the person repeats wudhu, he will be greatly rewarded.
As long as no act of worship has been performed with that wudhu, it is makruh to make a new wudhu.
If a person makes wudhu while bathing, he should read salât with that same wudhu without making a new wudhu unless it breaks.
If a person has read even just two rakâts of salât with the first wudhu, there is no problem in making a second wudhu and there is reward in making a second wudhu.

If someone's hands or feet are cracked and filled with wax, ointment, or medicine and removing it may cause harm, wudhu is regarded as complete if water is poured over it without removing the medicine.

If water did not reach the heels or some other place during wudhu and only after completing wudhu one realizes a place is dry, it is not sufficient to merely pass the hand over that place; water must be poured over it.
If there is a sore or wound and pouring water is harmful, water should not be poured and instead wet hand should be passed over the wound (masah).
If masah is harmful, that place should be left out.
If a wound is bandaged and it is harmful or difficult and painful to open the bandage, it is permissible to make masah on the bandage.
If it is not the case that opening the bandage is harmful or difficult, the bandage has to be removed and masah made on the wound.
If a wound is not under the entire bandage, after opening the bandage the unwounded portion should be washed if possible.
If it is not possible to open the bandage, masah should be made on both the wounded and unwounded portions.
For a fracture with splints and pads, as long as splints cannot be opened, it is sufficient to make masah over them.
For plasters, if masah cannot be made on the wound, the plaster should be removed and masah made on the gauze.
If there is no one to help in opening and closing plaster, it is sufficient to make masah on the plaster itself.
For bandages, splints, plasters, etc., it is preferable to make masah on the entire covering.
If making masah on the entire covering is not possible, it is permissible to make masah on more than half of the covering.
It is not permissible to suffice with masah on half or less of the covering.
If after performing masah the bandage or plaster opens and the wound has not healed, it should be re-tied and the previous masah will suffice.
If the wound has healed and there is no need to bandage it again, the masah will be broken and the portion should be washed and salât performed without repeating the entire wudhu.
Khilâl of the beard should be made three times after having washed the face.
Khilâl of the beard should not be made more than three times.
It is fardh to wash the chin as long as there is no hair of the beard on it, or if there is, it is so little that the skin can be seen.
It is fardh to wash that part of the lips which can be seen after the lips are closed.
If beard, moustache, and eyebrow hair is so thick that skin cannot be seen, it is not fardh to wash hidden skin because the hair is in place of the skin.
If beard, moustache, or eyebrow hair is thick enough that skin cannot be seen, it is wajib to wash the hair within the boundaries of the face.
It is not wajib to wash hair beyond the boundaries of the face.
If piles come out, wudhu breaks irrespective of whether it went back inside on its own or by pushing it back with a stick, cloth, or hand.
If semen comes out without any desire, wudhu breaks.
An example given for semen coming out without desire is carrying a very heavy weight.
Another example given for semen coming out without desire is jumping from an elevated place and due to shock semen came out.
If there is a defect in one's senses that does not reach the stage of insanity or unconsciousness, wudhu does not break.
If a person sleeps away and laughs in his sleep while in salât, wudhu does not break.
By laughing in a janaza salât or in a sajdah tilâwat, wudhu does not break irrespective of whether the person is mature or immature.
